b281889397b6eb84: STOCKHOLM: Sweden's central bank raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter point to 2% on Wednesday in a bid to combat inflation, and said further increases were likely.
The hike was the first in Sweden since September 2023.

The Riksbank said stronger economic activity, cost increases due to supply disruptions linked to the war in the Middle East, and a weaker krona meant inflation was expected to rise above the bank's 2% target.

"If the outlook for inflation and economic activity holds, it is likely that the policy rate will be raised further in the coming year," the Riksbank said in a statement after the widely expected increase.
"With this monetary policy, inflation is expected to stabilise around the target of 2% after a while," it said.
The bank said CPIF - the consumer price index with a fixed interest rate, its preferred inflation gauge that strips out the impact of floating mortgage payments - was 1.5% in September.
However, it said the rate was being held back by temporary fiscal policy measures, including a tax cut on food items.
"Excluding these, CPIF inflation was 3%," the bank noted.
The bank said "several risks" could affect its outlook, including supply disruptions and the possibility that Sweden's economy could grow faster than expected.
"There are also risks of weaker demand linked to the global economy, such as geopolitical uncertainty, concerns about AI investments, and weak public finances in certain countries," it said.
The interest rate had been held at 1.75% since September 2025.
Wednesday's increase was the first since September 2023, when it was raised to 4%, a 15-year high.

f42c17a0daabb0a0: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — The fourth phase of Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) cash aid, amounting to RM1.1 billion, is being disbursed starting today to over five million recipients nationwide, as part of ongoing efforts to assist the public in coping with the pressure of the cost of living.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the disbursement is being made in conjunction with the Deepavali celebration and covers recipients from various ethnic backgrounds.
He noted that this assistance reflects the government's commitment to ensuring that the welfare of the people particularly those in the low-income group remains a priority.

“Therefore, in conjunction with Deepavali, I am announcing that from today until November 6, a total of RM1.1 billion in STR aid will be distributed to more than five million people,” he said while speaking during a visit to the Deepavali Mega Bazaar 2026 in Brickfields here today.

Also present were Minister of Communications Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, Minister of Human Resources Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, and Minister of Digital Gobind Singh Deo.

Anwar, who is also the Minister of Finance, emphasised that the STR (Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah) assistance is not focused on any specific ethnic group, instead it is open to all citizens who meet the eligibility criteria.
He noted that the Indian community also benefits from this initiative, with over 630,000 recipients accounting for 7.4 per cent of the total number of STR recipients nationwide.

Meanwhile, the Prime Minister said the government’s cash assistance allocation has grown from RM6 billion under the “Bantuan Rakyat 1Malaysia” (BR1M) scheme in 2018 to RM8 billion under the “Bantuan Keluarga Malaysia” (BKM) scheme in 2022.
He added that this figure is set to rise to RM15 billion for STR and “Sumbangan Asas Rahmah” (SARA) allocations in 2026, before increasing further to RM16 billion under the 2027 Budget.
He remarked that this increase in allocation demonstrates the government’s commitment to strengthening the social safety net and ensuring that aid reaches those in need.

“So, you can make comparisons. You can also express gratitude. Some might say, ‘It existed before, too.’ That is true. But how much was it back then? RM6 billion. And how much is it now? RM16 billion for the people especially those in the lowest income bracket,” he said.

Meanwhile, in a statement today, the Ministry of Finance said STR payments to existing recipients will be processed from November 4 to 6, while new recipients and those whose appeals were approved will receive their payments starting November 16.
Of this total, 4.0 million are households with an income of RM5,000 or less, while 1.4 million are senior citizens without a spouse.
Based on eligibility categories, households will receive up to RM500, while senior citizens without a spouse will receive RM150.

MOF also said recipients with bank accounts will receive payments via direct credit to their respective accounts, while those without bank accounts may collect their payments in cash at any Bank Simpanan Nasional (BSN) branch.

Further information, status checks, and Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) regarding the STR can be accessed via the official portal at bantuantunai.hasil.gov.my, while information concerning SARA (Sumbangan Asas Rahmah) can be found at sara.gov.my. — Bernama

52fe13539c5c8c76: SHAH ALAM, Nov 4 — The Selangor state government has mobilised 7,677 personnel from various state agencies to prepare for disasters during the Northeast Monsoon (MTL), which is expected to continue until March 2027.

State Public Health and Environment Committee chairman Jamaliah Jamaluddin said the mobilisation involved the State Disaster Management Unit (UPBN), local authorities, district offices and relevant agencies to coordinate operations and monitor high-risk areas.

In a statement today, she said the operation was supported by 708 land vehicles, 247 water transport assets and various rescue equipment, including 5,739 tents, 1,950 life jackets, 141 water pumps and 20 drones.

According to the Selangor Drainage and Irrigation Department (JPS), the state is expected to receive 2,232 millimetres of rainfall this year, with 1,460 mm, or 65 per cent, recorded as at November 1. Rainfall of 268 mm and 230 mm is forecast for November and December respectively.
Jamaliah said JPS was monitoring flood risks through 221 rainfall telemetry stations, 124 water-level monitoring stations, 140 warning sirens and 72 IP cameras.

Based on 2025 data, JPS had identified 56 flood hotspots and 232 flood-prone areas, with Klang recording the highest number of hotspots at 13, followed by Petaling (11), Gombak (10) and Hulu Langat (nine).
She also cautioned residents in coastal and river estuary areas of Klang, Sepang, Petaling, Kuala Langat, Sabak Bernam and Kuala Selangor about the risk of high tides.
Meanwhile, 1,161 temporary relief centres (PPS) had been identified statewide, including 696 schools under the Education Ministry, 242 public halls and 135 community halls.
Jamaliah said agencies had been instructed to ensure the centres were safe, equipped with basic facilities and sufficient food supplies, while giving due attention to vulnerable groups.

She advised residents to monitor weather alerts through the JPS Public InfoBanjir portal and the Malaysian Meteorological Department’s (MET Malaysia) myCuaca 3.0 application, and comply with evacuation orders. — Bernama
337c472c1a7ba5dd: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Police have uncovered a suspected tax-stamp diversion scheme involving luxury liquor following the seizure of 370 bottles worth RM702,566 in the Klang Valley on Monday and yesterday.

The operation, Ops Taring Alpha 2, was conducted by the Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Investigation Intelligence (WCB/PSK) of the Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (JKDNKA), in collaboration with the Kuala Lumpur Federal Territory Customs Department.
WCB/PSK commander Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said the liquor, packed in 73 boxes, was seized during separate raids at a warehouse in Selangor and business premises in the capital.
He said initial inspections at the warehouse found that some luxury liquor bottles allegedly bore tax stamps or customs labels with lower duty rates than those applicable to the products.
“The modus operandi is believed to involve the diversion of tax stamps to evade excise duty payments, potentially resulting in revenue leakage,” he said in a statement today.
However, inspections at the second premises found that all liquor bottles bore valid tax stamps, with no offences detected.

Mohd Zaki said four individuals, including three Bangladeshis, were arrested to assist investigations under Section 15(1)(c) and Section 55B of the Immigration Act 1959/63, as well as Regulation 39(B) of the Immigration Regulations 1963.
The Customs Department is also investigating possible offences under Section 133(1)(c) of the Customs Act 1967. — Bernama
f41368190e09f311: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Three boat operators were among 38 Indonesian nationals detained by the General Operations Force (GOF) in an operation to curb migrant smuggling along the coastal area of Kampung Sungai Gatal, near Sabak Bernam, on November 2.

GOF Central Brigade acting commander ACP Awang Arfian Awang Bujang said all of them were detained in a raid under Op Taring Delta at about 4.30am while they were believed to be attempting to leave Malaysia via an illegal sea route.
He said the other 35 individuals arrested comprised 24 adult men and 11 adult women.

“The operations team also seized a fishing boat, a Mitsubishi engine and three mobile phones of various brands, which are believed to have been used as communication devices in the smuggling operation.
“The total value of the seizures is estimated at RM406,800,” he told a press conference here today.
He said the case was being investigated under the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007 (ATIPSOM) and the Immigration Act 1959/63.
Awang Arfian said the GOF Central Brigade recorded 171 cases involving migrant smuggling activities and immigration offences from January 1 to November 4 this year.
He said enforcement operations during the period led to the arrest of 898 individuals in the brigade’s area of responsibility, which covers Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka and Johor.

“Of the total, 33 cases were investigated under ATIPSOM, involving the arrest of 76 boat operators, while another 138 cases were recorded under the Immigration Act 1959/63, with 822 arrests,” he said.
He said the GOF would continue to intensify operations and intelligence gathering to combat migrant smuggling and other illegal cross-border activities.
“Members of the public with information on such activities are urged to channel it to the police for further action,” he said. — Bernama

09031b3641020cac: SEOUL: A backlash against President Donald Trump's Republican Party over rising living costs in the midterm elections could embolden countries around the world to resist his combative trade policies, which have raised prices for American consumers.

Democrats captured majorities in both the Senate and House on Tuesday, as US voters delivered a stinging rebuke for Trump's policies, specifically tariffs and the Iran war, which they blame for persistent inflation.

That could give countries more reason to slow-walk investment pledges they made to stave off tariffs, and hand economic rival China a perceived upper hand in ongoing trade talks, political analysts and economists said.

Trump's next major international outing will be a trip to Asia later this month, where he is due to meet with Southeast Asian leaders in the Philippines and then join the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen, China.
Japan and South Korea, America's closest allies in Asia, promised US$550 billion and US$350 billion respectively in US investments last year under deals with Trump.

"Democrats seem to perceive that the investment commitments were forced on allies," said Heo Yoon, economics professor at Sogang University in Seoul, adding that countries might now feel less pressure to fulfill such commitments.
But others cautioned that Trump, criticised at home, could squeeze allies harder abroad, pushing them to deliver pledged investments to show his policies are working.
“The tariff issue is not over. If Japan’s response is slow, calls for additional tariffs could resurface,” said Kazuhiro Maeshima, a professor of US politics at Sophia University in Tokyo.

South Korea has become a lightning rod for Trump's anger at countries he believes have not lived up to investment pledges made to stave off tariffs he says are needed to rebalance US trade with allies and rivals alike. Most recently, Seoul pushed back on Trump's assertions that it had agreed to fund Alaska LNG, a liquefied natural gas pipeline project.

While Trump can still wield executive power over tariff policy, Ban Kil-joo, international relations professor at Korea National Diplomatic Academy, said scrutiny from Congress over such projects could give Seoul "more valuable time" to review and assess them.
Trump tamed of unleashed?
For countries like India, still negotiating trade deals with the US, the midterm results could provide an incentive to adopt a wait-and-see approach, analysts said.

India's trade minister earlier this month said the first phase of an India-US trade deal was in the final stages of drafting, but reiterated that ​New Delhi would proceed only if it secures an advantage over competing exporters.
New Delhi and Washington agreed in February to a framework that reduced to 18% from 50% a punitive tariff on most Indian goods, imposed in August last year after an earlier round of talks collapsed.

After the midterms, the White House may face greater pressure to avoid a return to trade wars that could further raise costs for American consumers, said Tommy Xie, head of Asia macro research at OCBC Bank.
Others, however, warned against the possibility of Trump becoming more flexible.

"Countries such as India should remain cautious. A Democratic victory will not necessarily make Trump more accommodating towards any country,” said Rajiv Bhatia, a former Indian diplomat and distinguished fellow at Gateway House, a think tank.
Bhatia added that India should undertake greater diplomatic preparation and engage more actively with the US Congress to press its concerns on trade, tariffs and visa-related issues.
No free reign with Beijing
China, which has struck a fragile trade truce with the US that expires in January, will be thinking of ways to use Trump's political fragility to strengthen its hand in trade talks, analysts said.

"Xi Jinping will recognize that Trump's authority has been greatly weakened by these results, and will no doubt be thinking about ways of exploiting that," said Saul Eslake, an economist at Corinna Economic Advisory in Australia.
But others said Trump's travails are not necessarily good news for Beijing.

The US president has gone to great lengths to improve relations with Xi — including hosting him for a lavish state visit last month — and a Democratic-controlled Congress may constrain his ability to offer sweeteners for future deals.

"Democrats are unlikely to give Trump free rein on deals with Beijing," said Alicia Garcia-Herrero, chief Asia-Pacific economist at Natixis, adding that they had already criticized Trump's summits with Xi for limited substance on key issues like AI.

A Democratic Congress is more likely to support tighter tech export controls and scrutiny of supply chains for AI and semiconductors, which will give Trump less flexibility on concessions impacting those high-growth segments, she added.

China's foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning told reporters on Wednesday that the midterms were an internal matter for the US and that Beijing would continue to manage differences and expand cooperation with Washington.
6756fef22b509c02: KUALA LUMPUR: The government has cut its job creation target for the country's economic corridors by 71% for next year, despite aiming to attract more investments into these regions.
According to the economy ministry's budget estimates released on Oct 9, the target for new jobs will drop from 150,100 this year to 43,000 in 2027.
However, the target for realised investments will rise from RM91 billion to RM94 billion over the same period.

Several MPs, including those from Kubang Pasu, Langkawi and Rantau Panjang, raised the figures during the committee stage debate on the ministry's allocation in the Dewan Rakyat today and questioned the sharp drop.
While he did not give reasons for the drop, economy minister Akmal Nasir said the number of jobs created depended on the type of investment.
“Technology-intensive projects generally use automation and require fewer workers, but need more skilled and semi-skilled workers,” he said when winding up the debate.
Akmal said Kedah Rubber City had attracted five investors with a combined investment commitment totalling RM3.344 billion as of September.
He said another three potential investors, with a combined estimated investment value of RM450 million, were in talks with the authorities.
He also said the ministry's development allocation for Sabah would rise by 100.7% from RM87.1 million this year to RM174.85 million in 2027.
Among the projects he cited were a RM150 million project to expand Sepanggar port and RM9.85 million to upgrade a road to Kota Kinabalu Industrial Park.
Akmal said RM236.6 million had also been allocated to 13 state development corporations for 38 projects next year, with all 13 receiving funding.
He said Kelantan would receive RM57.5 million for seven projects, Kedah RM52.5 million for five, Pahang RM34.3 million for six and Perak RM18 million for two.
Selangor, which did not receive any allocation this year, was being considered for a RM5.77 million allocation to help small Bumiputera businesses.
f96110ac40434a67: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Government assistance for the Indian community is not only channelled through the Malaysian Indian Community Transformation Unit (Mitra), but also includes various initiatives in welfare, entrepreneurship, education and social development, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

He said such assistance was also provided through various government agencies and programmes, including the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) cash aid scheme, Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA), entrepreneurship financing through Tekun Nasional and Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia, as well as allocations for the development of Tamil schools and places of worship.

He said the government also planned to fully rebuild SJKT Ladang Pamol in Kluang, Johor, as well as establish six new SJKTs, including in Sungai Bakap, Penang and Klebang, Perak.
Meanwhile, the allocation for the maintenance and development of registered places of worship was also increased to RM80 million next year, compared with RM50 million annually since 2021.

cd6d63bfd38f0879: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 4 — The Court of Appeal was told today that the prosecution has yet to physically serve a notice of appeal on Muhammed Yusoff Rawther, a former research assistant to a politician, who is currently in the United Kingdom (UK).

Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) How May Ling told a three-member panel that authorities in the UK and Ireland had failed to locate Muhammed Yusoff or serve the notice on him, despite assistance being sought from Interpol.

“The prosecution was informed last month that efforts to locate the respondent (Muhammed Yusoff) had been unsuccessful. The authorities also had no information regarding his asylum application,” she said during case management before Justices Datuk Azman Abdullah, Datuk Hayatul Akmal Abdul Aziz and K. Muniandy.

The prosecution is appealing against the Kuala Lumpur High Court’s decision to acquit and discharge Muhammed Yusoff of charges of trafficking cannabis and possessing two imitation pistols at the end of the prosecution’s case, without calling him to enter his defence.
How said the respondent’s counsel had informed the court during an earlier proceeding that they were still in contact with him and had received instructions to represent him in the appeal.
The DPP said the prosecution was seeking another case management date to allow efforts to locate Muhammed Yusoff and serve the notice to continue.
It also applied for the proceedings to be conducted via Zoom so that he could appear online and confirm his whereabouts in the UK, facilitating service of the appeal notice.
On the Zoom application, Justice Azman said the case should not be treated differently from other criminal cases.
“I do not want to make an exception in this case. This is a criminal proceeding, and the respondent must appear physically in court. This court also does not want to set an unnecessary precedent.
“If the prosecution succeeds in locating him, bring him before this court,” he said.
Justice Azman also urged the lawyer to advise his client to return to Malaysia, given that they had a channel of communication with him.

Counsel Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali, representing Muhammed Yusoff, said he acknowledged that physical service of the appeal notice was a legal requirement under Section 314 of the Criminal Procedure Code.
However, he maintained that his client was not on the run but was in the UK to seek asylum.
The court fixed February 3 next year for further case management.
On June 12, 2025, High Court Judge Datuk Muhammad Jamil Hussin acquitted and discharged Muhammed Yusoff, 33, after ruling that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against him.
The court found that the prosecution had failed to prove, through witness testimony, that the accused had control, custody or possession of the two pistols and the drugs.

Muhammed Yusoff was charged with trafficking 305 grammes of cannabis found in a vehicle he was travelling in outside the surau at the Kuala Lumpur Police Contingent Headquarters at 10.15am on September 6, 2024.

The charge was brought under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, punishable under Section 39B(2) of the same Act, which provides for life imprisonment and not fewer than 12 strokes of the cane upon conviction.
He was also charged with possessing two imitation pistols by the roadside near a condominium in Jalan Bukit Kiara at 9.25am on the same day.
The charge was under Section 36(1) of the Arms Act 1960, which carries a maximum jail term of one year, a fine of up to RM5,000, or both, upon conviction. — Bernama

7df9b9e9aae557f8: JAKARTA, Nov 4 — An Indonesian military helicopter carrying eight people on a firefighting mission crashed in waters off Borneo island today, killing a crew member, the army said.

The Southeast Asian archipelago has for months been struggling to control wildfires that have burned through large swathes of Sumatra, Borneo and Papua islands, causing choking haze that drifted to neighbouring Malaysia, East Timor and Singapore.
The helicopter took off this morning from Seruyan district in Borneo’s Central Kalimantan province to fight fires in the Tanjung Puting National Park, an army statement said.
The park is home to animals including critically endangered Bornean orangutans.
“The accident occurred while the helicopter was scooping seawater for water-bombing,” the statement said.
“The cause of the incident is still under investigation.”
One crew member was killed while five others were rescued alive, said the army.
The statement did not provide any details about the condition of the two remaining crew members.

Aside from ground-based firefighters, Indonesia has also relied heavily on air operations to put out fires that have razed more than 1.9 million hectares in the nine months to September this year, according to deforestation monitor Nusantara Atlas.
The fires are driven in part by a strong El Nino weather phenomenon, which in Indonesia typically causes drought.
Experts say deforestation and peatland drainage is at the root of the destruction.

Pollution from smoke emitted by this year’s blazes caused an estimated 3,560 deaths in Indonesia in September alone, according to the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air, a Helsinki-based think tank.
More than 400,000 people in Indonesia have been treated for acute respiratory ailments caused by the toxic haze, the health ministry said today. — AFP

04da5d83e87717cb: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 4 — The Penang Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) is conducting an investigation to determine the actual cause of the landslide at Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, covering aspects such as safety, construction, and regulatory compliance.

State Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye said the investigation includes gathering information and statements from the developer, contractors, and consultants involved in the development project on the slope near the site of the incident.

“The Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) held discussions yesterday (Nov 3) with civil and geotechnical consulting engineers, the developer, and the contractor to investigate and understand the root cause of the incident covering aspects of safety, construction, design, and compliance with relevant regulations as well as to propose appropriate mitigation measures and site stabilization efforts.

“DOSH has requested that the developer submit Pre-Construction Information (PCI) documentation before commencing any mitigation work on-site,” he said when winding the debate on the Supply Bill and the 2027 Development Expenditure Estimates (State Budget 2027) at the State Legislative Assembly sitting today.

In the incident on October 25, a doctor, Dr Wong Kar Lin, 73, died after being buried in a landslide that affected his home, while his wife, Chang Mei Nuo, 68, and his mother-in-law, Wong Poh Lim (in her 80s), managed to escape safely.

Elaborating further, H’ng said the approved 35-story affordable housing project near the site does not exceed the 76-metre (250-foot) contour line while infrastructure development such as roads and utilities is permitted, subject to strict conditions outlined in the geotechnical report approved by the Committee for Development on Risky Land on April 10, 2023.

Additionally, he explained that the development approval for the site dates back to 1996, when the initial developer submitted an application for a proposed project consisting of medium-cost apartments and townhouses.

The planning permission application subsequently underwent several changes in terms of the developer and the proposed development plan before... The application for planning permission for the development of the affordable housing project was submitted in 2023.

“I wish to emphasise here that all decisions made were collective decisions of the government not merely the decision of the Chief Minister, but rather those of the State Authority and the Local Authority,” he stated.

In response to a query from Muhammad Fauzi Yusoff (PN-Sungai Dua), who interjected to urge the establishment of a State Commission of Inquiry (SCI) to investigate the cause of the tragedy, H’ng said the state government would first defer the investigation process to the Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) before considering such a measure.

He explained that the relevant documentation must be examined by DOSH, with technical advice sought from the Engineering Department of the Penang Island City Council (MBPP) specifically regarding geotechnical aspects to ensure that the proposed mitigation works are appropriate, before any further action is taken.

Previously, Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow asserted that the landowner and the developer of the condominium project must be held accountable, including regarding legal implications and the implementation of mitigation works to ensure the safety of the area affected by the landslide. — Bernama

52027d956993e01f: Fresh on the desktop this week is a new version of Enlightenment as well the continuation of noughties hero KDE 3, the Trinity Desktop Environment, for those who prefer things a little old school.

Enlightenment version 0.28 is the latest release of one of the older Linux graphical environments, which first appeared in 1997. Version 0.28 arrives nearly two years after the previous release – we reported on Enlightement 0.27 in January 2025. If you're not familiar with this venerable window manager, often referred to as just E, we refer you back to that article, which also explains Enlightenment's slightly strange version numbering scheme.

Last time around we noted that its single-line release notes really didn't give us much to write about. The development team has made up for it this time, with some 68 lines of changes. It's both the same old E, and simultaneously a modern tool: it is still an X11 window manager, but it can also act as a Wayland compositor if you prefer. It offers conventional stacking resizable windows, but also can act as a tiling window manager if you prefer. On recent distros, it can now talk to the Pipewire audio server, and it can also work with NetworkManager to control network connections. This version delivers preliminary support for NetBSD too.

This isn't really a tool for newbies or those looking for a simple easy desktop. A sign of its age is that the first-run wizard asks if you want windows to activate as soon as you move the mouse pointer over them. This was traditional 20th century Unix behavior, and in the early days of Linux it was called "focus-follows-mouse," but it's rarely seen today. E isn't a full desktop environment: it only offers a few of its own optional tools, such as the Ecrire text editor, Ephoto picture viewer, Evisum task manager, and Rage video player. Even its taskbar is optional. It is more like a basis for experienced users to customize and build their own environment around.

The Trinity Desktop Environment has a rather lower learning curve: TDE is a port of the final version of KDE 3 to modern Linux. Proving old school is still cool, the project – which keeps the look and feel of 2005-era KDE 3.5 alive – has just announced TDE release 14.1.7, with dozens of bug fixes and plenty of new features. Among these is a tweak to the kicker/taskbar: you can now scroll the taskbar using the mouse wheel, flicking through your open applications.This release drops support for Ubuntu 24.10 "Oracular Oriole" but adds support for the latest 26.10 "Stonking Stingray."

Forks of older versions by users disenchanted with new versions are a recurring feature of the FOSS world, but they often tend to peter out after a while. TDE is one of the exceptions: we first reported on a new release in 2021 and again in 2023. ®

9cc31730629426eb: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 4 — Police arrested 35 foreign nationals suspected of involvement in an online fraud syndicate specialising in love scams and gold investment schemes during raids on two residences in Bayan Lepas, near here, last Monday.

545726cbe77aae8a: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — The ringgit edged up against the US dollar and other Asean currencies at today’s closing ahead of Bank Negara Malaysia’s (BNM) Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) decision tomorrow.
BNM’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) will hold its sixth and final policy meeting of 2026 on Nov 5.
At 6pm, the local note rose to 4.0610/0660 against the greenback from yesterday’s close of 4.0735/0775
According to reports, research firms expect BNM to maintain the OPR at 2.75 per cent tomorrow and throughout 2027, supported by resilient economic growth and a manageable inflation outlook.
It said headline inflation is expected to remain comfortably within BNM’s projected range of 1.5 to 2.5 per cent in the near term.
On the external front, SPI Asset Management managing partner Stephen Innes said the ringgit was on firmer footing following the Democratic Party’s gains in the US Mid-Term Elections.

He said a Democratic sweep of US Congress could provide modest support for Asian currencies, including the ringgit, as increased political gridlock in Washington could reduce the likelihood of further US fiscal expansion, potentially weighing on US Treasury yields and the US dollar.
“However, for the ringgit to make more meaningful gains, we would probably need to see markets start pricing out some of the odds of a December US Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike.

“The complication is that President Donald Trump’s tariffs remain largely under presidential control, so the election result does not necessarily remove the inflation pressures that could prevent the Fed from shifting toward a more dovish stance. That may limit how far the US dollar can fall, at least initially,” he told Bernama.

Similarly, Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said market sentiment appeared to have improved following the US Mid-Term Elections result as the Trump administration could face greater legislative hurdles in passing new laws, although the US President retains veto powers.

“Consequently, the US Dollar Index (DXY) fell 0.46 per cent to 101.399 points. It is still too early to tell whether the elections result would see significant shift in US policies especially in relation to trade and the ongoing war in Iran.
“For now, markets are quite constructive which to some degree, may have resulted in improved risk appetite. Therefore, the ringgit was gaining by 0.20 per cent to RM4.06 today,” he said.

0d4f0f2456356663: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — A total of 864 high-profile individuals, including prominent figures (VVIPs), members of parliament and state assemblymen, have been identified for failing to pay Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) contributions for their domestic workers.

Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the figure was part of 10,033 employers of domestic workers found to have failed to comply with the contribution requirements, based on Perkeso’s preliminary checks as at November 1.

Asked whether any ministers were among the employers who had failed to comply, Ramanan revealed that individuals holding positions higher than Cabinet members had also been found to have committed the offence.

“Some are even higher-ranking than ministers. The 864 high-profile individuals include those holding key positions in the public and private sectors, as well as prominent figures, members of parliament, state assemblymen and other employers of domestic workers.

“The Ministry of Human Resources (Kesuma) views any failure to register domestic workers and pay their Perkeso contributions seriously,” he told a press conference after the presentation of Perkeso benefits to victims of the Nepal floods at Menara Perkeso here today.
Also present were Perkeso Board chairman Datuk Seri Subahan Kamal and Perkeso Group chief executive officer Datuk Seri Dr Mohammed Azman Aziz Mohammed.
Ramanan said all employers concerned, including VVIPs, had been given until December 7 to fulfil their contribution obligations, failing which action would be taken against them.

He said enforcement would begin with the issuance of compounds, while employers who continued to disregard the requirements could face a fine of up to RM10,000, imprisonment of up to two years, or both.

“We do not want to embarrass anyone. Please check whether you have paid or not. If you have, thank you. If you have not, please pay. No one is above the law. The law applies to everyone without exception.

“We cannot talk about workers’ welfare and rights if we fail to fulfil even the most basic responsibilities towards the workers in our own homes. Leadership by example must begin with compliance with the law,” he said.
Ramanan also disclosed that another 26,669 employers had been identified as having outstanding contribution records, which required further checks and follow-up action by Perkeso.

He said he had instructed Perkeso to take a firm stance in strengthening monitoring and enforcement against employers who failed to fulfil their responsibilities, adding that the main objective was not to impose compounds or fines, but to ensure that domestic workers received the social security protection they were entitled to. — Bernama
Socso is the English name for Pertubuhan Keselamatan Sosial (Perkeso), Malaysia’s Social Security Organisation.

76fc5027e2571ac4: Microsoft wants enterprise customers to start thinking about PC refreshes using the same mindset – and line in the budget – as AI investments. The problem? Rising component costs caused by the proliferation of AI datacenters mean many clients are delaying client refreshes.

In a call to arms, Microsoft became the headline sponsor of the Canalys Forum in Barcelona early last month for the first time ever. Redmond needs distributors and resellers that convene at the event annually to get behind Copilot, Cowork and, more generally, AI computers.
Mark Linton, corporate veep for Windows and Device Sales, took to the stage to preach to a room he is hoping to convert.
"What we're seeing is the tokenomics of [AI] is getting very challenging," he said. "Having agents working on frontier models quickly becomes very expensive."

Redmond's proposed solution is to use those massive LLMs where most needed, "the right model for the right job," running smaller models locally at the edge on Windows PCs. "My goal, if we're successful in pivoting Windows to the agentic platform, is to have PC spend be part of the AI spend versus just PC refresh budget," he said.

"In an AI hybrid world, you'll be able to use edge devices, powerful PCs with lots of memory, lots of capability to run your AI workloads that are appropriate right there on the device. You keep the data locally. Of course, you don't have the token cost of the cloud. You have better latency, and you have more control."
Copilot is merely a component. This is not only about customers using Microsoft "first-party software" – it's for all models and all agents to use Windows as the platform, added Linton.

Goodness knows, Windows does need a shot in the arm. Microsoft last week reported profit and loss accounts for Q1 of its fiscal 2027, ended September 30, and revenue in the Windows OEM and Devices division shrank 22 percent from last year to $3.55 billion. Microsoft warned revenue generated in its Q2 may be down 30 percent.

"Growth will continue to be impacted by elevated inventory levels, PC market demand and a prior year comparable that benefited from Windows 10 end of support," Microsoft CFO Amy Hood said on an earnings call.

Market watcher IDC said calendar Q3 PC shipments sank to 62.7 million units, down 20.1 percent year-on-year, translating into 15.8 million fewer sales into distributors' warehouses. Tough macroeconomic conditions coupled with rising memory costs mean tough times for the PC industry.

Omdia – which owns Canalys – said: "The impact of upstream component cost increases has now fully worked its way through to end-market pricing, with consumers and IT decision-makers responding accordingly."

Reg readers know why component costs are going up. The datacenter construction frenzy meant memory chip makers could make more money from higher-margin HBM than conventional DRAM, prompting them to prioritize production of the former.

But AI PCs have been a tough sell from the start, as higher prices and a lack of killer applications meant many customers delayed purchases. Microsoft has to convince the market of the benefits – including trade customers as well as those in charge of procurement at enterprises.
Once more, the pitch for AI PCs

Back at the Canalys Forum, Microsoft's Linton claimed customers mulling AI PC purchases want better productivity, to reduce costs, to innovate, and to be able to use these computers securely and at scale.

Microsoft is going to invest heavily in Windows from both the platform capability and security to enable these ends. So, if you are a Microsoft partner, you'll be able to run Windows and secure agents at the operating system level with Agent 365, with Intune, or with Entra.

Linton added: "We announced in June some of the technology in Windows, in particular Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC). And so essentially you can virtualize agents, and then you can use Intune to give them policy. And so other platforms, you have to manage agent by agent. Windows, you'll be able to do it policy-based, much like you manage people and network resources.

"You will have agents for all, and you need to know how to manage them, track them, audit them, and then ensure that they're contained in the right way. So we're doing that at the operating system primitive level."
Some of the quality control issues that have dogged Windows may give some sysadmins pause for thought about the grand claims made by the Windows exec.

Still, Microsoft is on a mission, and it knows how to attract thousands of resellers by dangling financial incentives in their direction. Linton said it is pumping money into channel programs, including AI-readiness funded headcount with "top partners" to "get this hybrid AI story moving."
Microsoft wants the channel to deploy AI internally too, "especially for your sales team" because "if they're using it, they're able to sell it."
Dell isn’t hopeful of an uplift in PC demand this year. David Kennedy, chief financial officer, said sales will remain "compressed."

"The reality is most enterprises this year for their IT budgets are sweating those assets out a little bit more and what dollars they have, they're trying to build out their infrastructure side," he told the Citi TMT conference in September.

"As we go forward, I think you'll see it [become] a little bit more robust. Our main focus will be on those higher ASP (average sales price) commercial boxes as part of the AI storyboard that's there."

He reckons there are more than 400 million PCs owned by customers that are "over four years old", and with the "cheapest token being closest to the data, none of those installed base PCs will have the battery life or the power to do AI workloads on them. So there is a pent-up demand that we believe will come once it stabilizes and once IT budgets get a little bit more settled and expanded."
Will 2027 be the year of the AI desktop? The Reg suspects not, though readers can do what they always do and speak their brains in the comments section. ®
c9a67bff41d827f7: 65 maritime workers certified, and 10 local companies recognised under the RM245.468 million Kuala Kedah RoRo Terminal project

KUALA KEDAH, Nov 4 — Technology Depository Agency Berhad (TDA), through the Industrial Collaboration Programme (ICP), has recorded a 100 per cent certification success rate for 65 maritime workers, while recognising the participation of 10 local companies in the Kuala Kedah Passenger, Cargo and Roll-on/Roll-off (RoRo) Terminal development project.

The achievement marks a milestone in TDA’s efforts to ensure that strategic government procurement generates long-term benefits through skills development, industry participation and the strengthening of local capabilities.

All 65 participants successfully obtained the Mate Domestic (Open) Certificate, with the certificates presented by Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook during the Maritime Competency Recognition and Local Company Empowerment Ceremony at the Kuala Kedah Passenger Jetty Terminal on November 2.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook during a site visit to review the upgrading works at the Kuala Kedah Passenger Jetty Terminal, accompanied by Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, Datuk Seri Jana Santhiran Muniayan and Mohamad Rafidi Mat Dahan. — Picture courtesy of Technology Depository Agency Berhad

The ceremony was also attended by Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, Ministry of Transport Secretary-General Datuk Seri Jana Santhiran Muniayan and TDA Chief Executive Officer Mohamad Rafidi Mat Dahan.

The certification represents the first milestone under the ICP initiative, “Future-Ready Seafarers Through Professional Certificates and Competency Programme for Domestic and International Maritime Standard”, implemented in collaboration with Sunissa Sdn Bhd, the ICP provider for the Kuala Kedah terminal project.
Transport Minister Loke said the development of skilled maritime personnel must progress alongside infrastructure improvements and greater participation by Malaysian companies.

“The maritime industry requires a competent workforce and a strong ecosystem of local companies capable of meeting operational standards. Through the ICP, government procurement can be translated into skills development, knowledge transfer and more meaningful industry participation,” he said.
In his officiating address, Loke also emphasised that infrastructure development alone was insufficient without a competent workforce, adherence to safety standards and operational discipline.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook receives a briefing from Sunissa Sdn Bhd on the upgrading works at the Kuala Kedah Passenger Jetty Terminal, together with Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, Datuk Seri Jana Santhiran Muniayan and Mohamad Rafidi Mat Dahan. — Picture courtesy of Technology Depository Agency Berhad

He highlighted the benefits of the Mate Domestic (Open) qualification, which provides a broader scope of competency than the Mate Domestic (Limited) certificate, allowing qualified operators to undertake maritime activities across Malaysian waters, subject to the Marine Department Malaysia’s regulations.
The qualification allows fishermen and boat operators to develop their skills, explore wider employment opportunities and potentially increase their income.
The 65 participants comprised members of the Kuala Muda Fishermen’s Association, Kuala Kedah Fishermen’s Association and Pantai Merdeka Boat Operators’ Association.

Training was conducted by Polaris Maritime Training Academy Sdn Bhd, a training centre recognised by the Marine Department Malaysia, across three sessions in Alor Setar in February, April and June 2026.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Technology Depository Agency Berhad CEO Mohamad Rafidi Mat Dahan delivers his remarks at the Maritime Competency Recognition and Local Company Empowerment Ceremony, held at the Kuala Kedah Passenger Jetty Terminal. — Picture courtesy of Technology Depository Agency Berhad

TDA Chief Executive Officer Mohamad Rafidi Mat Dahan said the achievement demonstrated how the ICP translates government procurement commitments into tangible outcomes for Malaysian industries and communities.

“This recognition signifies more than the completion of a training programme. It demonstrates how collaboration among the Government, implementing agencies, training providers, and industry can systematically build local capability. TDA will continue to ensure that strategic procurement delivers competencies, capacity and enduring value,” he said.
Beyond maritime competency development, the ICP also supports the participation of Malaysian companies in the Kuala Kedah terminal project’s supply chain.
Ten local companies were recognised during the ceremony, reflecting the programme’s focus on developing local industry.

Under the project’s localisation and subcontracting component, Malaysian companies participate in activities including machinery rental, soil investigation, marine and onshore piling, construction-material supply, building systems and electrical works.

Their involvement is intended to strengthen domestic capabilities, facilitate knowledge and technology transfer, and create opportunities for local businesses to participate in larger infrastructure projects.
The Kuala Kedah RoRo Terminal project, valued at RM245.468 million, commenced in April 2024 and has an implementation period extending to September 2027.
Upon completion, the upgraded terminal is expected to accommodate up to 3,000 passengers, compared with approximately 800 previously, and allow three large passenger vessels to berth simultaneously.

As an agency under the Minister of Finance Incorporated, TDA facilitates and monitors the implementation of Malaysia’s ICP, ensuring that strategic government procurement delivers measurable and sustainable value through industrial capacity building, human capital development and technology transfer.

The Kuala Kedah initiative demonstrates how infrastructure investment can be leveraged to develop a more capable maritime workforce while creating opportunities for Malaysian businesses to strengthen their participation in the national supply chain.
For further information on TDA and the Industrial Collaboration Programme, visit www.tda.my.
2432851be061162c: LONDON: Global stocks and the dollar recovered on Wednesday from lows hit overnight after Democrats won control of both the Senate and the House in the US midterm elections, which has fuelled fears that rapid AI sector growth could be hamstrung by regulatory scrutiny.
In a major setback to President Donald Trump, Democrats scored sweeping victories in Republican strongholds for the first time in generations.
The breadth of the party's success was underscored by gains in districts long considered safely conservative, highlighting a political shift that may have caught some investors off guard.

"Democrats pulled off a double victory in the US midterm elections that few saw coming at the onset of the year. The blue wave means the federal government is sure to be divided on most issues," Deborah Cunningham, chief investment officer, global liquidity markets at Federated Hermes, said.
"That typically creates a blockade against new legislation — an environment which broad financial markets traditionally view favourably as variables decrease."
Opinion polls have shown Democratic voters favouring more control over AI, and investors expect the Democratic-controlled Congress to apply more scrutiny to the sector.
AI stocks in Asia initially led the decline in equity markets, while bonds and safe-haven currencies such as the Swiss franc gained.

By the time the bulk of the midterm results had filtered through in the European morning, equities had turned higher. MSCI's All-World index was up 0.13%, while Europe's STOXX 600 which has acted as a hedge against AI-related risks, was up 0.5%. US stock futures also ESc1, NQc1 edged into positive territory, having fallen by as much as 2% overnight.
Shares in Elon Musk's Tesla and SpaceX, which he intends to merge, were down around 4.5% to 5% on Europe's Tradegate platform, compared with declines of around 0.3% to 0.9% for other Big Tech stocks.

"Overall, these results have had a mild impact on markets so far. Investors will move on from trading the uncertainty of the election results to trading the reality of what they mean for policy," XTB research director Kathleen Brooks said.

"This is bad news for Tesla and SpaceX on Wednesday, but the semiconductor names, the backbone of the AI trade, could brush off concerns about AI regulation and continue to move higher after Tuesday’s stunning rally for the sector," she said.

The AI boom has helped propel global markets in recent years, driven by heavy spending from tech giants racing to build data centres and expand computing capacity. That has made investors acutely sensitive to anything that could derail the technology's rapid expansion.
The election outcome could also hold broad implications for the US fiscal outlook as well as sectors such as defence, healthcare and banking.
Futures on the small-cap Russell 2000 index RTYc1, which is more exposed to the US domestic economy, were last up 0.7%, having lost 1% earlier.
Investors flock to safe havens
Treasuries rallied as investors expect gridlock in Washington to cut government spending, with AI regulation also possibly slowing growth and reducing the need for rate hikes.
The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note was down 3 basis points on the day at 4.92%, having fallen as much as 6 bps to a low of 4.89% overnight, which, in turn, weighed on the dollar.

"Bonds are coming out as the clear winner as markets put the AI trade on the chopping block and embrace the higher possibility that further tax cuts are put on ice and government spending slows," Prashant Newnaha, senior rates strategist at TD Securities in Singapore, said.
In currencies, the dollar weakened broadly, leaving the euro up 0.4% at US$1.133 and the pound up 0.5% at US$1.348 GBP.

The yen and the Swiss franc, both safe-haven currencies, also notched up gains. The Swiss franc was the standout performer, with the dollar down 0.6% against it at 0.8163 francs. The dollar also fell 0.4% against the Japanese yen to 158.12.

In the oil market, prices were choppy on Wednesday after they hit a four-week low in the previous session as investors weighed talks to end the wars in Ukraine and Iran against worries that recent attacks in both conflicts could further disrupt supplies. Brent crude LCOc1 was down 0.4% on the day at US$103.17 a barrel.

ffabf4bddfa3c81a: Schneider Electric sees no slowdown in its datacenter business, but says operators must be more open with communities about the power, water, and land their projects will consume.
As a supplier of electrical infrastructure, cooling, and power distribution equipment, Schneider has a direct view of operators' spending plans – and a commercial interest in continued construction.

Steven Carlini, vice president of innovation and datacenter, said Schneider's pipeline showed no slowdown. "And Schneider has a lot of agreements, supply chain agreements with the larger datacenter operators."
Reports earlier this year suggested only half the capacity planned for 2026 is actually under construction in the US, and land being cleared for new bit barn projects has plateaued.
Carlini nevertheless said US companies were building as fast as they could, contrasting that with planning bureaucracy and other obstacles in Europe.

"But the one thing that I think is going to be the biggest change is the level of transparency from the operators when they're trying to secure permits and when they're requesting power," Carlini said.

"The way the model traditionally worked in the US is the operators would negotiate with the local jurisdictions that were responsible for issuing the permits, and there would be non-disclosures involved, almost universally. So the residents where these datacenters were going to be built had no visibility into these projects until construction started."
Opposition to datacenter construction has grown in the US. Campaign groups called for a moratorium on new facilities late last year, and New York state imposed a halt this summer.

The sheer scale of the new builds has also alarmed many folk, with Meta's Hyperion facility, for example, planned to reach 5 GW of power capacity and cover an area equal to a significant chunk of Manhattan.

A recent survey by think tank Pew Research Center found that Americans are increasingly wary of datacenters, with more than half saying they are bad for the environment, bad for household energy bills, and consume water resources for cooling.
In response, companies building and operating compute sheds need to be more upfront about what effect their plans will have on the local area, Carlini said.

"They're going to have to disclose where the power is going to come from, how they're going to get the power, their water usage, their carbon emissions, the efficiency of the datacenter, where it is going to be located physically, the noise levels of the facility, the water sources, which is a big one, and how much water they're going to use is another big one that operators have traditionally not been very forthright in publishing."

In Virginia – the world's "datacenter capital" – an ex-water sustainability program manager at AWS is taking his former employer to court over claims it published false and misleading statements about water use in the state.
Carlini expects permitting requirements to force greater disclosure, followed by reporting obligations once facilities are operating.

"And then they're going to have to report it as part of regulations during operations as well, so it's not going to be a case of here's our prediction, and then you get the permit and you never have to report again," he said.
Datacenter owners and operators must win hearts and minds as well, Carlini added, a point already recognized by some in the industry at an event last year.

"From a public relations perspective, that's another area where the operators really need to focus, because in many cases they've taken the position that they're benefiting the community," he said. "Those days are gone, so the operators are going to have to, from a PR perspective, engage with the local residents more amicably."
People using Facebook or Gmail doesn't mean they'll welcome a datacenter next door, Carlini told us.
"So it's going to have to be more like 'Here's how we're going to help,'" he said. Operators would need to acknowledge residents' concerns and explain any benefits, such as tax breaks or lower costs.
For AI facilities, Carlini expects more attention to token-processing performance and efficiency, rather than power capacity alone.

"I think we're going to start to see more and more focus on tokens per watt, tokens per dollar, and even datacenters could be sized in tokens as a performance metric for the IT rather than just the power metric," he told us.
"I think the industry has suffered in the past because datacenters have always just been sized in power consumption, and that gave little idea what it was producing and what value [it] was adding."
For more on the economics of tokens in AI processing, readers can refer to our article on this topic from earlier this year. ®

b949b5b4384e41cf: NAIROBI: Corruption is costing Kenya billions of dollars each year in lost revenue, inflated business costs, and lost earnings for workers, while taking a huge toll on investment and economic growth, the World Bank said in a report published Wednesday.

Kenya suffers corruption at every level of society -- from endless petty bribes paid to traffic police, to vast procurement scandals that go to the top of government, and it has contributed to massive protests over the past two years.

The World Bank report said the east African country is among the most corrupt of its peers among lower middle-income countries, and estimates that the governance weaknesses are adding around 370 billion shillings (US$2.8 billion) every year to Kenya's fiscal deficit, equivalent to 2% of GDP.
This figure, which its authors describe as "conservative", comes from lost taxes, inefficient public spending, higher borrowing costs, and other issues caused by corruption.

Ordinary Kenyans are furious over the levels of graft -- the issue was a major part of the massive protests in mid-2024 when the government tried to raise taxes -- and the World Bank notes that its people would be far more willing to contribute if they trusted their leaders.
The report's authors hope Kenya’s politicians will wake up to the advantages of tackling the issue.

Its modelling shows Kenya's economy could be more than 20 times larger by 2035 if it introduced the sort of anti-corruption reforms seen in countries like Ghana and Senegal, and add 7.7 million more and better jobs.

"Kenya has a lot of the ingredients that it would take to be a really leading country in the region. And it should make good on that promise, both for its own citizens and for the neighbouring region. And it's feasible," Verena Fritz, lead governance expert for World Bank Kenya, told reporters.
The World Bank finally approved its latest lending package to Kenya in June after it was stalled throughout 2025 because the government was dragging its feet on anti-corruption measures.
It has insisted on new rules against politicians' conflicts of interest, a new electronic procurement system, and the passing of a Whistleblower Protection Bill that has been stalled for years.
For now, though, the report showed that corruption is taking a massive toll on many aspects of Kenya's development.

Kenya's electricity is far more expensive than some of its peers, it says, largely because only 24% of 42 power purchase agreements examined in a 2021 study were known to have gone through a competitive process.

Contracts for big infrastructure projects are often far pricier than they should be: the bank notes that the Nairobi-Mombasa railway line cost around a third more per kilometre than a similar line in neighbouring Tanzania.
Cleaning up just 10%t of procurement losses could save Kenya 120 billion shillings ($930 million) a year, it added.

The issue is only getting worse: a World Bank survey found that 39% of Kenyan firms considered corruption a major or severe constraint to doing business in 2025 -- up from 25% in 2013 -- and 36% said they had been asked for a bribe at least once in the last year.

2b2c21c556dea1c3: COPENHAGEN: Novo Nordisk's Wegovy pill beat third-quarter (Q3) sales forecasts on Wednesday, a test of whether the Danish drugmaker's new oral weight-loss drug can help it regain lost ground to rival Eli Lilly.

Novo, which at one point became Europe's most valuable listed company on booming Wegovy sales, is also trying to narrow a gap to Lilly, whose rival Foundayo pill is winning a growing share of new prescriptions.
Novo also raised its 2026 adjusted sales and adjusted operating profit to a range of between +2% to -2% at constant exchange rates, from a previous forecast of a 0% to 6% fall.
It was the third time the company raised its full-year guidance.
Adjusted operating profit was 31.72 billion Danish crowns, above the 28.39 billion projected by analysts and up 27% in constant exchange rates from a year earlier.
Adjusted sales were 79.20 billion crowns against 73.22 billion expected.
"Growth was led by our obesity portfolio, with continued uptake of Wegovy pill in the US and encouraging early launches internationally," CEO Mike Doustdar said in a statement.
19906427673aea7a: FRANKFURT: BMW on Wednesday reported shrinking earnings the day after issuing its second profit warning of the year as Chinese competition shakes the global car industry.
Net profit for the third quarter fell about 15% 1.45 billion euros (US$1.61 billion), BMW said, and sales fell almost 6% to 30.45 billion euros.

BMW on Tuesday issued its second profit warning of 2026, warning that costs associated with a production ramp-up as well as higher-than-expected severance payments could push its core car business into an overall loss for the year.
"Current developments in our industry call for decisiveness," BMW CEO Milan Nedeljkovic said Wednesday. "We will therefore specifically intensify and accelerate structural measures."

Like its peers Mercedes-Benz and Volkswagen, BMW is cutting jobs to try and bring costs down as lower-cost and more advanced Chinese rivals have largely muscled their German counterparts out of China and are now stepping up exports to Europe.
BMW's vehicle deliveries in China -- last year already at their lowest level since 2017 -- fell another 24.8% in the quarter, the firm said, dragging overall global deliveries down 6.3%.
The group, which apart from its namesake also includes Mini and Rolls-Royce, has promised to shift more of the supply chain for its Chinese vehicles into China in a bid to build back market share.

07e5df5b0b383c36: Donald Trump’s Republican Party has received a stunning rebuke in the US midterm elections. Republicans went into the evening hoping that the polls might be wrong and that they could at least cling on to control of the Senate. But by midnight in Washington, the GOP was staring down what looked like its worst defeat in 50 years. Republican losses were not just confined to the type of swing districts that parties usually worry about on election night. The scale of the losses was staggering. They lost Senate seats in deep red states such as Texas and South Carolina. They lost districts they had gerrymandered and in which they were supposed to be unbeatable. They lost seats that even the sharpest analysts thought were safe. Why? For months, surveys have shown that voters are fed up with high prices, with the war in Iran, and with what is increasingly being talked about as the Trump administration’s corruption. A president who was narrowly elected on the promise of a steady economic hand instead spent two years pursuing an extreme ideological agenda favoured only by a minority of Americans. He ignored what voters were saying, and now they have delivered a harsh verdict. Read more: What recent polling suggests will happen in the US midterm elections But these results have implications beyond just the remainder of Trump’s presidency. They break some of the patterns that have defined American politics for decades. Democrats are suddenly winning in places where they have been counted out for a generation. Suddenly, the American political map looks different. Take Texas. The last time a Democrat won election as a senator there was 1988. Democrats have not won a presidential election in Texas since Jimmy Carter in 1976. Yet last night, Democrat James Talarico powered to a convincing victory. If elections in Texas become politically competitive on a permanent basis, it will become much harder for Republicans to take the presidency in the future. The Republican Party will now be looking nervously towards the 2028 election. For the first time since 2016, there is likely to be a serious debate within the party about whether to move on from the aggressive nationalism and bigotry of Trump’s “Make America Great Again” movement. Democrats, meanwhile, face their own questions about how to capitalise on their victories. Foreign policy futures But for the rest of the world, change might not come so quickly. Despite the fact that his party has suffered this electoral setback, Trump remains president until 2028. And because despite its constitutional role in declaring war and ratifying treaties, Congress tends to be less involved in foreign policy, there is still a lot that he can do with that power. Indeed, US presidents whose parties perform badly in midterm elections often become more active in foreign policy than they had previously. With the chance of passing a significant domestic agenda mostly beyond their reach, they have a more time on their hands to think about America’s relations with the rest of the world. The same is likely to be true of Trump. The fact that the midterms are over also means that Trump no longer has to be so careful about the political consequences of his actions. As the midterm elections got closer, the president has backed down from major military confrontation with Iran and sought a truce in his tariff wars. Now, with political constraints lifted, he could become more erratic and unpredictable. Congress would not be completely powerless to stop him, at least in theory. But most actions it can take – such as cutting off funding for the war with Iran or seizing tariff power back from the president – require margins of control in both chambers that Democrats are unlikely to have, despite their formidable victories. They would need to have a two-thirds majority to override an almost certain presidential veto on any attempt to pass laws to achieve these outcomes. So a key question is whether this midterm drubbing was serious enough to make some Republican members of Congress get serious about joining Democrats in restraining Trump. Something that Democrats will definitely be able to do is launch all manner of investigations into the conduct of the Trump administration and some of its officials. Their efforts are likely to focus on the war with Iran, Trump’s personal financial dealings with foreign leaders, and the management of the Pentagon by secretary of defence Pete Hegseth. Hegseth, indeed, could be an early casualty of these efforts – there is speculation that he will resign or be fired rather than face possible impeachment. But ultimately a change of direction in US foreign policy depends on the decisions of Trump himself. A changing of the guard among his advisers, or in Congress, can only do so much to influence a president who has never willingly submitted to constraint. The world should prepare itself for the possibility that a politically wounded and angry Trump could now decide to vent his frustrations abroad. Andrew Gawthorpe is a senior fellow at the Foreign Policy Centre in London.
